citation.title: The activities of NiO, CoO and FeO in silicate melts

reported_gamma_spread.interpretation: Reported pooled spread; not relabelled as a confidence interval.

derivation.premise: Holzheid, Palme, and Chakraborty report the pooled CoO liquid-standard activity coefficient from 76 silicate-melt experiments; for trace Co, use the dilute relation.
derivation.units_check: gamma and oxide mole fraction are dimensionless, so activity is dimensionless.

limitations: The pooled coefficient is provisional for a specific melt composition.
The dilute-concentration upper limit is not numerically specified by the source.
Other major-oxide composition effects are not parameterized.

standards.citation: Gurvich, Veyts, and Medvedev, Thermodynamic Properties of Individual Substances, Volume IV, Table 1334, CoO(cr,l).

derivation.premise: Table 1334 gives paired CoO crystal and liquid rows at 2090 K, with equal F = S - (H-H0)/T values; it labels the liquid heat capacity and fusion enthalpy as estimates.
derivation.algebra: Delta_H_fus = 156.405 - 116.405 = 40.000 kJ/mol; Delta_S_fus = 183.223 - 164.085 = 19.138 J/(mol K), consistent with 40000/2090 = 19.139 J/(mol K). For the liquid branch, H_l(T)=H_cr(Tm)+Delta_H_fus+Cp_l(T-Tm), S_l(T)=S_cr(Tm)+Delta_S_fus+Cp_l*ln(T/Tm), and G_l=H_l-T*S_l.
derivation.units_check: Enthalpy differences are kJ/mol before conversion to J/mol; Cp*(T-Tm) is J/mol; Cp*ln(T/Tm) is J/(mol K).
derivation.sanity: At Tm=2090 K, equal printed F values and Delta_H_fus approximately Tm*Delta_S_fus make G_l(Tm)=G_cr(Tm).

flags: This is an opt-in trace-solute estimate and does not modify the default melt or gas tables.
The CoO(l) standard is already present in the shipped gas table; its source values are documented here without changing that table.
